Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zugrpc 0.0.0.9000

  • Metadata named r, re or req is sent, instead of failing the call with an error from zuhttp (#81).

  • A metadata name given more than once is sent once, its values joined by commas, instead of failing at call time. Every user-agent given is kept, and an empty one no longer adds a leading space (#82).

  • Requests no longer ask for HTTP content coding (accept-encoding: gzip), and a response with one is not decoded. content-length and accept-encoding are reserved names. A client passed to grpc_channel() may not set a reserved header, and its query is dropped (#83).

  • grpc_channel() refuses a URL whose host or port cannot be used, with zugrpc_error_argument, instead of every call failing as UNAVAILABLE (#84).

  • grpc_keepalive() refuses values outside 1 ms to 2147483.647 s, which zuhttp would refuse or clamp, and prints its values in full (#85).

  • A positive deadline below a femtosecond is sent as 1n, not 0n (#87).

  • A stream decides its status as a unary call does. A status in the headers counts only when no body came, a status in the trailers wins over a body that ends inside a message, and an OK status in the headers no longer makes an HTML body acceptable. The not-gRPC error keeps the first 1 KiB of the body (#58).

  • A stream returns the complete messages that arrived before a broken one, then raises, however the server’s bytes were split (#76).

  • A warning while a stream ends, such as from undecodable -bin trailers, can no longer make a failed stream read as a clean end (#77).

  • A unary response larger than max_message is still UNAVAILABLE for a 503 and a protocol error for a body that is not gRPC, instead of RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Its condition carries http_status (#79).

  • One error detail that does not decode no longer discards the whole google.rpc.Status. It is kept as it came, with a warning (#80).

  • A stream’s $status() names how it ended, such as "CANCELLED" or "DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", and a stream of a closed channel prints as cancelled (#86).

  • A comma-joined -bin value with a trailing comma gives an empty last value, as a leading comma gives an empty first one (#88).

  • A call or stream with no deadline no longer fails with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED after 30 seconds, zuhttp’s default timeout (#23).

  • A server’s malformed grpc-message or -bin metadata no longer hides the call’s status. A -bin value that is not base64 is dropped with a zugrpc_warning_metadata warning, and comma-joined values are split (#25, #26).

  • grpc_close() no longer closes the connections of the zuhttp client a channel was built on, or of other channels built on it (#27).

  • Every condition of a call carries method, and http_status once there is a response (#28).

  • A stream that failed raises the same condition on every later $next_message(), instead of reading as a clean end (#35).

  • Metadata named host, or a connection header HTTP/2 forbids, is an argument error. A user-agent you set is sent before zugrpc’s own instead of being replaced (#36).

  • A method name must use protobuf name characters (#50).

  • Reading many small messages from a stream no longer slows down with the number in each read (#34).

  • grpc_channel() opens a channel to a gRPC server over cleartext HTTP/2 (http://) or TLS (https://). It can build on a zuhttp::zu_client() you supply, so proxies, TLS settings and test transports carry over. grpc_close() closes it.

  • grpc_call() makes a unary call. It returns the response message with its initial and trailing metadata, and raises zugrpc_error_status, with a class per status code, when the call fails. Responses that are not gRPC or break its framing raise zugrpc_error_protocol.

  • A failed call’s condition carries details, the google.rpc.Status decoded from the grpc-status-details-bin trailer, with each error detail such as ErrorInfo unpacked. A trailer that does not decode is a zugrpc_warning_details warning, and the status is kept.

  • grpc_stream() makes a server-streaming call. Its $next_message() returns one message at a time as it arrives, so the server sends only as fast as you read. $cancel() stops the call and keeps the connection. grpc_close() cancels a channel’s open streams, and a stream that is no longer referenced is cancelled when it is garbage-collected.

  • A call whose deadline has already passed fails with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED without being sent.

  • grpc_keepalive() sets HTTP/2 keepalive for a channel. By default a connection idle for 60 seconds is checked with a PING before its next call, as Spark Connect’s Python client does.

  • Each call no longer spends about a millisecond rebuilding the user-agent string.

  • zugrpc_info() reports the zuhttp version, whether it speaks HTTP/2, and its TLS backend.

  • Failures below gRPC raise zugrpc_error_transport, which is also zugrpc_error_unavailable. A timeout is DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, and an interrupt raises zugrpc_error_interrupt.

  • grpc_status_codes() lists the 17 gRPC status codes.

  • The gRPC wire format, internal for now: message framing, metadata with -bin values in base64, the grpc-timeout header, grpc-status and grpc-message decoding, and the HTTP-status fallback.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
